descriptionEn: Free diagnostic unit exam for Unit 1: Communication & Relationships covering reading comprehension, vocabulary, and grammar in High Note 11.
text: We know that some animals understand basic1 instructions, allowing travellers to control their horses or camels, for example. But although some of the more intelligent2 animals can figure out3 what we want them to do, we have long assumed that communication with - and between - animals must be limited. However, thanks to the work done by the naturalist4 Jane Goodall since the 1960s, we should take the possibility seriously that some animals can both take in5 what we are saying and get across complex6 ideas. As a child, Jane loved reading books about a fictional1 character called Dr Dolittle, who could talk to animals. Perhaps this is what inspired her to go to Africa when she was in her 20s. Here she came across2 a scientist who asked Jane if she might want a job observing3 chimpanzees in the wild. She immediately said yes. She went with her mother to the shores4 of Lake Tanganyika in Tanzania to start her new job, and it was not long before she made out5 a group of chimpanzees in the trees around an area now called the Gombe Stream National Park. How could a young English woman with no scientific training possibly make contact1 with a group of wild chimpanzees? At first, the animals ran away as soon as they saw her. But maybe because she knew very little about these wild animals, it is highly likely that her calmness gained2 their trust. It was only later that Jane would learn how dangerous they could be. She saw that different groups of chimpanzees had battles in which they tried to wipe out3 the rival4 group. But before this, her studies showed her that the chimpanzees could clearly communicate, allowing them to groom5 and help each other, share food as well as have arguments. Jane pointed out6 that the animals couldn't communicate using language like people, but they could communicate by touch and sound. Amazingly, she also realised they could use sign language. At this time, people believed that only humans could use tools, but Jane watched chimpanzees using sticks to take ants from a tree, and then used the sticks to feed the ants to their young. Through her work, Jane spelled out1 to the scientific community for the first time that animals, too, could use tools. Jane went on to write a number of books about her work. As well as explaining chimpanzees' highly developed social behaviour, she taught us that they are omnivores2 (people used to think they were vegetarian). In 2002, she became a UN Messenger for Peace. In my opinion, Jane Goodall brought about3 a complete change in the way people understood how animals can communicate. Since her work in Tanzania, naturalists have continued to study different forms of communication between animals such as whales and elephants, who can pick up4 sounds made by other whales and elephants over large distances. I feel that we may well learn even more about animal communication in the future.

How did Jane Goodall manage to gain the trust of the wild chimpanzees?
choices: By waiting quietly every day in the forest until they got used to her.
By offering them food and playing with their young.
By building a shelter near their natural habitat.
By imitating their sounds and behaviors.

questions.question: The writer believes we may learn even more about animal communication in the future. In your opinion, why is it important for humans to understand how animals communicate?
choices: Understanding animal communication helps us protect endangered species and their habitats.
It is not important because humans are fundamentally different from animals.
Animals do not have meaningful communication, so studying it is useless.
It is only useful for training pets to obey commands.

questions.question: According to the text, what two things did Jane Goodall's work with chimpanzees demonstrate about their ability to communicate?
choices: that chimpanzees have a complex system of communication and that they can show emotions
that chimpanzees are good at climbing trees and finding food
that chimpanzees prefer to live in isolation and avoid humans
that chimpanzees cannot learn new skills from other animals

questions.question: Write down the sentence which states that Jane Goodall's work caused a major change in how people viewed animal communication.
choices: Because of Jane's work, people had to change the way they thought about animals.
Chimpanzees use a variety of sounds to warn others of danger.
The chimpanzees eventually allowed her to come closer.
Her discoveries were published in scientific journals worldwide.
